title: Nf3t's Vintage Story Wiki manifest
description: vs-manifest.json: what `npm run download` fetches (the vanilla dedicated server and mods) and extra items/blocks `npm run ingest` should always include. Mirrors the VsManifest interface in src/ingest/types.ts; keep the two in sync. Also the config file vsdev (apps/vsdev) reads from the working folder or a parent: the location fields below set where the game, mods, releases and mod pages are (after flags and environment variables, before the folder defaults). A mod project's file may contain only those.

$schema.description: Path to this schema, so editors like VS Code validate and autocomplete the file.

serverBranch.description: cdn.vintagestory.at release channel the server is downloaded from. Default: stable.

serverVersion.description: Vanilla dedicated server version to download, e.g. "1.22.7". Changing it changes the CI cache key, so the next build re-downloads everything. Default: 1.22.7.

gameVersion.description: The game version (same as serverVersion; this name reads better in a mod project). vsdev uses it to pick mod releases and as the download version.

gameKind.description: Which download `vsdev game` and `npm run download` fetch when not told: the whole client (textures, DLLs; includes the server) or the smaller dedicated server. The wiki uses "server".

gameDir.description: The game install (client or server), relative to this file. After --game-dir and $VINTAGE_STORY; default ./vintagestory (an old ./vs_server is still read). Client and server share this location; gameKind decides which is downloaded.

dataDir.description: The game data folder whose Mods/ vsdev installs into and the wiki reads, relative to this file. After -p/--data-dir and $VINTAGE_STORY_DATA; default: ./Mods.

releasesDir.description: The built mod zips `vsdev moddb` works on, relative to this file. Default ./Releases (the VS mod template's output).

pagesDir.description: The mods' ModDB page sources (`vsdev moddb`), relative to this file. Default ./moddb.

prodWikiUrl.description: Where the production wiki is deployed (GitHub Pages). The build info page links to it, even on a local build, and `vsdev search` asks this wiki (after --wiki and $VSDEV_WIKI_URL; default: the project's own wiki).

mods.description: Mods from mods.vintagestory.at to download and ingest alongside the vanilla game, like a requirements file: `vsdev manifest freeze` writes the mods in a Mods or Releases folder into it, `vsdev manifest install` (or `vsdev download`) downloads them. A mod present in Mods/ but missing here is skipped by ingest.

modid.description: The mod's id on mods.vintagestory.at (its modinfo.json `modid`), e.g. "betterruins".

version.description: Release version to pin, exactly as listed on the mod's page (e.g. "0.6.4"). Omit to take the latest release.

src.description: For a mod you develop yourself: the folder holding its source (the one with modinfo.json), relative to this file, e.g. "TranslocatorLocatorCmdMod". Maps the modid to its folder name; vsdev reads it with `modSourceDirs`. The mod is still downloaded from ModDB like any other entry unless you leave it out of the downloads yourself.

wikiIncludeItems.description: Wiki only (this project's generated site; vsdev ignores it): items/blocks to always give an /items/ page, even when no recipe, drop table, worldgen rule, trade list, or NPC dialogue reaches them (e.g. static translocators). Each entry is a "domain:code" glob matched against every concrete item/block variant code; `*` is a wildcard. Leaving out the "domain:" prefix matches any domain. Ingest warns about patterns that match nothing.

items.description: "domain:code" glob, e.g. "survival:statictranslocator-*". Vanilla items/blocks mostly live in the "survival" or "game" domain; mod content uses the mod's own domain.

screenshotsDir.description: vsdev only: where `vsdev screenshots` writes its PNGs, relative to this file. Default ./screenshots.

screenshots.description: vsdev only (the wiki ignores it): schematic screenshots `vsdev screenshots` renders, e.g. for a ModDB page. Blocks are drawn in block colors, chiseled blocks as cuboids; entities (players, creatures) inside a schematic are not drawn.

name.description: File name of the PNG without .png; `vsdev screenshots <name>` renders just this one.

schematic.description: The schematic to render (or use `model`): a file relative to this file, or `domain:path` of a schematic inside the game install's assets or a mod zip/folder in Mods/ (e.g. "betterruins:schematics/ruin.json").

view.description: Camera angle: a view name, or a direction [x, y, z] from the center (y up, +z south, +x east). Default "default".

model.description: Instead of `schematic`: a shape (model) file to render with its real textures (needs the game client): a file relative to this file, or `domain:path` in the game's assets or a mod (e.g. "survival:shapes/block/machine/statictranslocator/normal.json").

scene.description: Instead of one `schematic` or `model`: several parts placed together in one image, e.g. a player in armor next to a broken translocator. Positions `at` are in blocks (x east, y up, z south).

model.description: A shape file (relative to this file) or `domain:path` in the game's assets or a mod; placed with its block corner at `at`.

player.description: The seraph player body in a pose, dressed in worn items and holding items. Its own front is west (-x).

wear.description: Worn item codes, e.g. "armor-body-antique-forlorn-pristine". Their shapes hang on the body's bones, and the body parts they disable (hair...) are hidden.

hold.description: Item or block code held in the right hand, e.g. "rod-cupronickel".

holdLeft.description: Item or block code held in the left hand.

holdScale.description: Multiplier on the size of held items (default 1); they grow about their own center, so they stay in the hand. The game draws most items small there, so raise it for an image.

animation.description: An animation of the player body (idle1, insertgear, helditemready, wave...), held at `frame`. Default: the rest pose.

frame.description: The animation frame to show (30 per second).

at.description: Position in blocks [x, y, z]: a model's block corner, a player's feet.

facing.description: Player only: the direction it looks.

rotationY.description: Turn about the vertical axis in degrees, counter-clockwise seen from above (a player at 0 looks west).

animation.description: Model only: an animation of the model, held at `frame`.

output.description: Where to write the PNG, relative to this file, instead of <screenshotsDir>/<name>.png (e.g. "MyMod/Screenshots/Main.png").

title.description: Large text drawn over the image.

titleSize.description: Title height as a fraction of the image's shorter side (default 0.075; the subtitle is 0.6 of it). Raise it for a small icon, e.g. 0.17 on 128x128.

subtitle.description: Smaller text under the title (e.g. "by Nf3t").

logo.description: An image (PNG, JPEG, SVG, WebP) drawn over the image, relative to this file.

textAt.description: Where the title block goes. Default top-left.

logoAt.description: Where the logo goes. Default top-right.

reflection.description: Add a faded, flipped reflection under the subject, which falls in the part of a ModDB card its text covers (use with a preset or `safe`, so there is room below).

background.description: Background color (any CSS color, e.g. "#1d3b2a"). Default dark grey.

height.description: Height in pixels when not square; `size` is then the width (1920 x 1080 suits ModDB). Default: same as size.

preset.description: Sizes for ModDB: modicon 128x128 transparent (the game's icon), moddb-logo 480x480 and moddb-logo-wide 480x320 (a mod card covers the bottom part and the top-right corner, so the subject is framed above that). Explicit size, height, safe and background win.

safe.description: Fractions (0 to under 0.9) of the image to keep clear on each side; the model is framed in the rest, and a logo-only icon fills it.

size.description: Width and height in pixels. Default 1280.

floor.description: Draw a one-block grid at ground level.

maxY.description: Leave out blocks above this y (a cutaway).
